topology_reasoning.device: Low-loss waveguide crossing with lens-shaped (elliptical) mode-expander tapers — four-fold symmetric, one arm per port (N/S/E/W).
topology_reasoning.how_it_works: A direct crossing of two single-mode wires scatters strongly at the intersection. This design expands each of the four access waveguides through a lens/ellipse-shaped taper so the mode is wide, flat-phase and self-imaging at the crossing point; the expanded beam crosses the orthogonal arm with minimal diffraction into it, then the symmetric taper refocuses back into the narrow wire. Black = material on layer (1,0).

pixel_evidence.peak_flat_region_um: r=0.70..0.90 from center (~0.2 um flat top)
pixel_evidence.profile_shape: widening is faster-than-sine, consistent with an elliptical (quarter-ellipse) width profile

function_defining_knobs: stub_width_um (access waveguide width — sets the guided mode)
lens_max_width_um (expanded beam width at the lens waist — sets self-imaging quality at the crossing)
taper_up_length_um / taper_down_length_um (adiabaticity / focal condition of the lens taper)
topology_reasoning.plan: One parametric arm = straight stub + elliptical up-transition + short straight at max width + elliptical down-transition ending at the center; four rotated copies unioned. Iterate on taper lengths / max width / center tip width against IoU diff.

iterations.change_made: Initial build: stub + quarter-ellipse up/down transitions + flat top, 4 rotated arms. (First run hit the 2-dbu port-width snap error; widths snapped in _xs.) Diff: blue crescents on every lobe flank — tapers far too slender.

Root cause found: gf.path.straight defaults to npoints=2, so the transition width callable was sampled linearly. Dense paths (npoints=201) + empirically fitted profile w0+(w1-w0)*sin(pi*s/2)^0.8 (fit to per-column target widths). Diff flipped to a thin red rim (slightly fat).

taper_shape_exp 0.86 — best; kept. Also made the script contract-compliant: GDS + lengths.json written next to the script via __file__, with_metadata=False so gdstk top_level() sees the real cell (kfactory $$$CONTEXT_INFO$$$ was the only top cell otherwise).

knob_verification.note: verify_knob_response's pass criteria are MZI-shaped: (a) lengths.json delta_length_um must move by delta_um — identically 0 for a 4-fold symmetric crossing (both through-paths change together), and (b) area growth must equal width_um*delta_um — assumes the knob lengthens ONE single-width waveguide, but every knob here touches all 4 arms. Both checks were run honestly and the raw area numbers prove the knobs move real geometry.

lens_max_width_um.interpretation: primary function knob; +0.2 um on the lens waist grows layer-(1,0) area by 1.002 um2 — real geometric response across the 4 lobes

stub_length_um.interpretation: area growth is exactly 4 stubs x 0.236 um x 0.5 um = 0.472 um2 — geometry responds precisely as physics predicts, 4x the single-arm contract expectation
